scope: Question design and response boundaries; external venues do not establish this restaurant's amenities or policies.

sources.title: Owner confirmation in this conversation
sources.supports: Drawing activities, toys, a play corner and a children's menu exist. No details about supervision, dishes, prices or age limits were provided.

sources.title: Configured synthetic restaurant profile
sources.supports: Opening hours, declared menu/diet/allergens, dogs policy, booking duration, maximum party size and fictional venue disclosure.

sources.title: Shared restaurant call and reservation policy
sources.supports: Supported actions, later consent after a delivered recap, owned cancellation, unknown information handling, language and conversation state.

sources.title: Visit Estonia places to eat with children
sources.supports: Family visits raise distinct questions about play areas, toys, drawing, children's food and seating. Amenities described for listed businesses cannot be copied into our venue profile.

sources.title: Eesti Lasterikaste Perede Liit family friendly label statute
sources.supports: The label has its own assessment and permission process. Its criteria motivate questions about seating, changing facilities, waiting time, activities, serving children earlier, parking and stroller storage. Four confirmed amenities do not prove certification.

sources.title: Põllumajandus- ja Toiduamet food information guidance
sources.supports: Food information must be accurate and understandable. Ingredient allergen declarations and possible unintended presence need separate handling. Catering and distance selling require relevant food information. This supports asking the kitchen rather than guaranteeing allergy safety.

sources.title: Visit Estonia travel options for people with disabilities
sources.supports: Guests should check specific facilities and communicate needs beforehand. Accessibility questions should name the route, entrance, seating and toilet requirements instead of assuming a single yes/no label is enough.

sources.title: Häirekeskus emergency number 112
sources.supports: 112 is the emergency number for urgent danger to life or health and for police/fire assistance. An urgent restaurant turn should direct the caller to emergency services and nearby staff, without pretending the bot has called them.

sources.title: Andmekaitse Inspektsioon telephone recording guidance
sources.supports: Recorded voice is personal data. Processing needs a lawful purpose and basis, transparency and minimisation. The restaurant must provide its actual recording, retention and rights contact facts; the bot cannot invent these.

sources.title: TTJA submitting a consumer dispute
sources.supports: Start by raising a complaint with the trader. Restaurant complaint answers should identify the actual contact/process and avoid inventing a refund, compensation decision or completed complaint submission.

sources.title: Street Burger operator FAQ
sources.supports: Published restaurant FAQs include bookings, walk-ins, groups, vouchers, delivery, dietary preferences and allergens. These are question categories only; the operator's thresholds, suppliers, prices and rules are not ours.

sources.title: Tallink Hotels family restaurant article
sources.supports: An operator describes toys, drawing, play spaces and children's menus separately. The article contains a dated campaign and is used only to develop family question categories.

sources.title: UK government consumer food allergy guidance
sources.supports: Ask about ingredients, preparation and cross-contact before ordering. Used as background for operational questions; no UK legal requirement is asserted for this Estonian profile.
